glm.feedback:
The diff is substantial and largely faithful to the spec. I traced the move-map logic through the keystone gate, `changed_catalog`, `ac_history`, `fr_history`, and the `fr_split` report, and the acceptance items 1–5 each have direct code plus tests. Findings:

- Category: test · Severity: medium
  File: shared/scripts/tools/tests/test_keystone_ac_moves.py:60-64 (and shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_keystone_core.py:150-151)
  Finding: The new test `test_a_moved_and_reworded_criterion_keeps_its_old_links_for_the_binding_check` only asserts `cs.moved == {...}`; it never runs `evaluate_keystone`. The `_keystone_core` change (looking up base links under the pre-move id) — the piece the round-1 review flagged as the medium-severity fix — is untested. If someone later reverts that two-line lookup or swaps the tuple order, every test in the suite still passes while the gate mis-judges the link counts of a moved+reworded criterion (exactly the false "added bindings" / missed-regression the fix was for).
  Suggestion: Add a test that builds a repo where the old id has base links and the moved criterion is reworded, runs `evaluate_keystone`, and asserts AC-2 passes (or fails) based on the old-id link count.

- Category: edge-case · Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/lib/fr_split_report.py:36
  Finding: `new_spec = next(iter(result["files"].values()))[1]` picks the first entry of the files dict and assumes it is the spec file the new rows were written into. This holds only by insertion order inside `plan` (the spec entry must be inserted first). If file ordering ever changes (e.g. the tags rewrite is recorded before the spec, or the spec lands in a second file for cross-file splits), `_row` returns `""` and the operator-facing "table row" line silently goes blank — the report claims to show the copied row but shows nothing, with no warning.
  Suggestion: Key the spec explicitly (e.g. pass `rel_spec` in the result, or filter `result["files"]` to the spec path) instead of relying on dict order.

- Category: spec · Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/lib/spec_chain.py:225-236
  Finding: Acceptance item 3 says "`ac_history` of the old and the new id returns the same runs", but alias joining happens only when `spec_acs is None`. Any existing caller that passes a pre-computed `spec_acs` dict silently gets no move-map joining — the old and new id return different histories for that caller. The docstring documents the limitation, but it is a contract asymmetry: same API, different answer depending on an optional argument.
  Suggestion: Either read the move map independently of `spec_acs` (it only needs the spec texts, not the catalog), or assert/annotate that the passed-in form is the legacy path. Reading the map separately is cheap and removes the asymmetry.

- Category: edge-case · Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/lib/ac_record.py:101-110 (same rule in verifiers/_keystone_criteria.py:84-91)
  Finding: The "real move" rule (`target must not exist at base`) misreads a legitimate single-commit sequence where a target criterion is deleted and its number immediately reused as the move destination: base has `FR-01.03.AC01` (old text), head deletes it and moves `FR-01.01.AC01` onto `FR-01.03.AC01`. Both readers report removed+changed instead of moved/unchanged. `fr_split` never produces this (it mints fresh numbers), so this only bites hand-written cuts — consistent with the documented "hand-written row" tradeoff, but it is a wider class than the docs imply.
  Suggestion: Acceptable as documented; consider noting "reuse of a freed number in the same commit" in the known limits rather than only "hand-written row onto a living id".

- Category: test · Severity: low
  File: shared/tests/test_fr_split_tool.py:225 (`test_the_cut_skips_a_number_origin_main_already_uses`)
  Finding: The test asserts `"FR-01.04" in out` but never asserts `FR-01.03` is absent from the new-ids line. A broken `origin_numbers` (e.g. returncode mishandling, wrong ref) that picks FR-01.03 anyway could still print FR-01.04 elsewhere (e.g. in a problems note) and pass.
  Suggestion: Assert the new-ids line exactly, e.g. `"...new ids ...): FR-01.04"` and that `FR-01.03` is not among the chosen ids.

Security: no issues — subprocess calls use argument lists without shell, regex inputs are escaped, no untrusted data reaches sensitive sinks beyond reading repo-local files.

Overall assessment: the implementation matches the spec's five acceptance criteria, the tricky "claimed target / hand-written row" logic in `changed_catalog` is sound and tested, and the residual gaps are an untested core-gate lookup and small report fragilities — ship-with-fixes, with the `_keystone_core` test gap the one worth addressing before PR 2 depends on this.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
